account: Today I have kept my appointments and am back at the office just before sixteen-thirty. The unusual business is a large gathering being prepared in the town hall for eighteen. Yesterday I saw both the builder and the innkeeper depositing bread in a hall table chest, and lanterns were already placed. Today the neighbour told me that two hundred fresh loaves had been verified at the hall this morning and guests need bring nothing; that is her report, not a count I made myself. She has been spreading the innkeeper's invitation. The builder personally invited me for eighteen, said the innkeeper would escort me, and deliberately asked to keep the occasion's details until then. The secretary reports that the innkeeper called it community hospitality, with the programme announced at eighteen and no prepared remarks needed. Thus the builder, innkeeper and neighbour are involved in organizing or publicizing a substantial, intentionally surprising feast. It may be a celebration for the community, perhaps one especially involving me, but I do not yet know its purpose. I should not treat that guess as established fact. I also heard townsfolk mention a bridge or port change at the bakery, but I have no verified explanation of such a change. No council letters had reached the secretary at our thirteen o'clock appointment, and I still have not received a full grain-stock report. I intend to keep the sixteen-thirty office appointment and attend the hall gathering at eighteen to learn what the organizers have planned.
